 Value-added tax refunds reached 99% of the 2026 forecast.
 With the vigorous implementation of the document processing mechanism and the strong application of information technology, in 2026, value-added tax refund procedures recorded significant improvements, considerably shortening processing time and freeing up working capital for businesses.
 Báo Nhân dân • 14/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Leaders of the Tax Department and experts participate in a discussion session at the annual Tax & Legal Institute 2026 conference. Photo: CTV File routing: Complete first, then check later. 
 The Ministry of Finance stated that tax refunds have been slow compared to requirements in recent times. In the context of businesses having difficulty accessing capital, slow tax refunds also affect business development.
 To address this situation, the Ministry of Finance has decisively directed the streamlining of value-added tax refund applications. Accordingly, businesses with a good history of legal compliance are placed in the green channel, accounting for approximately 80% of the total number of applications.
 Based on the streamlined process, 88% of green channel applications are processed for tax refunds within 7 working days, with the remainder subject to pre-audit and post-refund procedures. As a result, the average processing time for tax refund applications has been reduced to approximately 40 days, compared to around 50 days previously.
 In the coming period, the management agency will continue to promote the application of information technology to classify dossiers more accurately. Thanks to streamlining and promoting digital transformation , tax refunds have reached nearly 99% of the 2026 budget allocated for tax refunds, an increase of over 40% compared to the same period. Notably, 100% of tax refund dossiers are received and processed electronically.
 Besides the progress in disbursement speed, the legal framework for tax refunds has also been synchronously improved to reduce administrative procedures. From July 1, 2026, the process of preparing value-added tax refund applications will be implemented according to the new regulations in Circular 89/2026/TT-BTC of the Ministry of Finance detailing some provisions of the Law on Tax Administration and Decree No. 252/2026/ND-CP of the Government detailing some provisions and measures to organize and guide the implementation of the Law on Tax Administration.
 These regulations have significantly reduced the number of documents taxpayers must submit, standardized new declaration forms, and adjusted the method of requesting tax refunds for export activities and investment projects, reducing some components of the application that must be submitted separately, making the process easier for taxpayers.
 You may also like However, the risk in tax refunds remains high, as evidenced by the fact that in just ten months of 2026, tax authorities rejected over 10 trillion VND in refunds due to incomplete documentation and the need for invoice verification. Given these challenges, the task of reforming administrative procedures and applying technology in the tax sector must meet the requirements of both strictly protecting the state budget and creating the most favorable conditions for citizens and businesses.
 Shifting the focus to risk management 
 Speaking at the recent annual Tax & Legal Institute 2026 conference, Director of the Tax Department Mai Xuan Thanh stated that accelerating the value-added tax refund process is one of the key solutions to free up financial resources and support businesses in maintaining and expanding their operations.
 Along with the administrative procedure reform process, the tax sector is changing its approach to tax inspection and auditing, shifting from periodic to risk-based management. 
 A view of the annual Tax & Legal Institute 2026 conference. Photo by CTV. Under the new method, tax authorities utilize big data systems from financial reports and related information to analyze and assess risk levels, thereby accurately identifying key areas for inspection and gradually reducing on-site audits at taxpayers' premises. All assessment results are updated and stored in the company's risk profile for subsequent management purposes.
 During this process, the tax authorities intensified their efforts in disseminating information, providing guidance, engaging in dialogue, and sending early reminders and warnings to businesses so that they could proactively address potential issues, rather than waiting until the tax authorities conduct an inspection to discover and correct errors.
 Providing timely information and guidance helps businesses better understand compliance requirements and minimize potential problems that may arise in fulfilling their tax obligations.
 The head of the Tax Department also noted that simplifying the required documents does not mean relaxing the legal conditions for tax refunds. Businesses must still fully meet the conditions stipulated by law, ensuring the accuracy and legality of invoices, documents, and declared information. In particular, businesses that comply well are not exempt from inspections and audits.
 You may also like To effectively adapt to changes in tax policy, each business needs to proactively improve its internal management capabilities, perfect its accounting system according to prescribed standards, and ensure the accuracy and consistency of financial data right from the initial accounting stage.
 From the perspective of the regulatory authorities, the issuance and adjustment of tax policies are also planned with a reasonable roadmap to give the business community sufficient time to prepare and comply.
 In the coming period, the tax sector will continue to improve the tax refund process towards transparency and convenience, strengthening the application of technology and data, and gradually limiting human intervention in the processing of applications. Simultaneously, it will implement an automated tax refund process, in which the system automatically connects data, analyzes, compares, and classifies risks, helping tax officials focus on cases that truly require verification.
 BICH NGAN
